name: agent-browser
description: agent-browser — drive a real headless Chrome: open pages, snapshot the accessibility tree with @eN refs, click, fill and submit forms, read and extract content, take screenshots and PDFs, record video, and test web apps through the agent-browser CLI.

settings.label: CLI version
settings.description: The npm version of agent-browser that Install puts in place, e.g. `latest` or `0.41.0`. Each CLI version pins its own Chrome build. Press Reinstall after changing it.

settings.label: Chrome sandbox
settings.description: Chrome's own process sandbox. Many servers cannot provide it (containers, VMs, Ubuntu 23.10+ with AppArmor restricting user namespaces) and Chrome then refuses to start.

options.label: Auto (decided at install)
options.description: Install launches Chrome once with the sandbox and once without, and runs without it only if the sandboxed launch fails. Press Reinstall after the host changes.

options.label: Always on
options.description: Never pass --no-sandbox. Chrome will not start on a host that cannot sandbox it.

settings.label: Allowed domains
settings.description: Optional. Comma-separated domain patterns (e.g. `example.com,*.example.com`) the browser may reach; navigation and page traffic anywhere else is blocked. Empty means any site. While set, saved-state restore, Chrome profiles and CDP attach are refused.

settings.label: Mark page content
settings.description: Wrap text that comes from web pages in boundary markers, so the agent can tell page content (which may contain injected instructions) from the tool's own output.
